text:
Following multiple fire incidents across Mumbai over the past two days, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) on Monday imposed a ban on the use of rockets and similar aerial firecrackers across the city until November 25.
The decision comes after major fire incidents occurred due to bursting of firecrackers at different locations, according to Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB).
On Sunday, 142 fire incidents were recorded in a single day, of which 137 were caused by firecrackers. Two women sustained injuries in these incidents, said MFB. The latest was the fire at Noorbaugh market in Dongri on late Sunday.
Also Read: 10-year-old boy dies after firecracker bursts in his hand on Diwali in Delhi’s Narela
The prohibitory order, signed by additional municipal commissioner Prajakta Lavangare-Verma in her capacity as chairperson of the Urban Disaster Management Authority came into immediate effect on November 9. It extends to both public and private spaces, including residential buildings, terraces, rooftops, balconies, courtyards, parking lots and slum settlements.
The civic administration cited the city’s dense population, high-rise buildings, narrow roads, slum settlements and concentration of residential and commercial establishments as factors that make aerial fireworks particularly hazardous.
The order said that when rockets and similar skyward-launching fireworks are ignited, their burning debris can fall on building rooftops, balconies, windows and combustible materials, potentially triggering fires and endangering human lives and property.
Also Read: Diwali eye safety: Doctor shares precautions to prevent firecracker injuries and how to protect your eyes
A senior civic official told HT that the decision was taken due to the uncertain nature of such firecrackers. “They don’t have a set path, and can travel anywhere. The wind movement can easily lead to ignition wherever it finds combustible material, hence banning would make sure that fire due to firecrackers would come to a halt,” said the official.
Thane also imposed a similar, albeit longer, prohibition. In an order dated November 9, district collector and chairman of the District Disaster Management Authority Dr Shrikrishna Panchal banned the use of rockets and similar aerial firecrackers across the entire district until January 8, 2027. The order came after 11 fire incidents were reported across Thane on Sunday.

In Mumbai, deputy commissioners of police, assistant commissioners and the fire brigade have been directed to ensure strict enforcement of the prohibition. The BMC clarified that the ban is restricted to rockets and similar aerial fireworks, while the use of other firecrackers will continue to be governed by prevailing laws, court orders and directions issued by competent authorities.
Osama Rawal is a trainee correspondent at HT Mumbai. He covers Asia’s largest civic body , the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), he reports on the decisions taken by the administration and statutory bodies,how these decisions shape the city, and their impact on the lives of ordinary mumbaikars. He is particularly interested in how citizens’ movements influence and redefine urban governance in the maximum city. He firmly believes that the only way to report the BMC is through the lens of people,rather than the other way around. He also covers environment ,but his reporting extends to virtually every major development in the city, from monsoon to worsening air quality to chasing human interest stories in everything that happens in the city. His reporting combines extensive field work with data,aiming to produce stories that are both deeply reported and evidence backed. He holds a bachelor’s degree in Political Science from Elphinstone College and is pursuing an LLB from the University of Mumbai. when he is not reporting you can find him buried in obscure religious and political texts,and finding evidence as a critical thinker and non conformist to back his what he considers ‘highly nuanced’ arguments.
